Success, an empty local set, parameter failures, and a missing receipt are all strictly read-only: no resource, receipt, or audit event is created or modified, and the existing package export, stateless verification, impact search, identifiers, UTC fields, and error JSON are unchanged.
- `GET /v1/impact-import-reconciliations?local_available=...&matches=...&limit=...&cursor=...` — read-only, paginated reconciliation of every registered impact-import receipt against the current local revocation-impact set. The request carries no body: any body bytes (even whitespace, arbitrary bytes, or malformed JSON) are `422 validation_error`, rejected before any query parameter, cursor, receipt, or local impact is read. The success body is compact UTF-8 JSON (compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII) terminated by exactly one newline, with members in exactly the order `items`, `count`, `next_cursor`. Each item is the existing single-receipt public view (`id`, `checkpoint_version`, `impact_count`, `impacts_digest_hex`, UTC `received_at`) followed by exactly `local_available`, `local_checkpoint`, and `matches`; the imported impacts array and every raw signature, payload, content, or evidence byte are never returned. Every receipt is reconciled at read time under exactly the single-receipt reconciliation rules: `local_checkpoint` is the four-field checkpoint computed over the complete, unfiltered local revocation-impact set (identical for every item; an empty local set still yields its deterministic checkpoint), `local_available` is `true` exactly when that local impact set is non-empty, and `matches` is `true` only when the receipt's `checkpoint_version`, `impact_count`, and `impacts_digest_hex` all equal the local checkpoint fields. Receipts are returned in stable creation order (`created_at`, with the persistent insertion order as a same-timestamp tiebreaker that survives a restart). The optional `local_available` and `matches` filters are each provided at most once and accept only the lowercase literals `true` or `false` (blank, capitalized, numeric, or other spellings are `422`); an absent filter imposes no restriction and the two combine as logical AND against the fields computed at that read. `count` is the filtered total covering every page, independent of the page returned. `limit` is a pure decimal integer from 1 to 100 defaulting to 50; `cursor` is an opaque HMAC-signed server token in its own `iir1` family, bound to both effective filters (including `null` filters) and the effective limit, so continuation pages repeat and omit nothing, replaying a cursor returns the same page, the final page carries `next_cursor: null`, a cursor at or past the tail returns empty `items` with the filtered `count` and `null`, and a query with no match returns `{"items": [], "count": 0, "next_cursor": null}`. The first page carries no `cursor`; a continuation carries the previous response's `next_cursor` with the same query conditions. Blank/illegal/repeated/undeclared parameters, an empty/whitespace-only/malformed/tampered/cross-family/foreign/filter-or-limit-mismatching `cursor`, and any non-empty request body are all `422 validation_error` — parameters, the body, and the cursor are validated before any receipt or local impact is read, a failure never returns partial results, and nothing is silently defaulted or normalized. The listing is strictly read-only: success, empty results, and failures create or modify no receipt, resource, or audit event, and the import, the single-receipt read, the receipt search, the single-receipt reconciliation, the package export, the stateless verification, and the existing error JSON are unchanged. Non-`GET` methods on this route are rejected with `405 method_not_allowed`.

## Impact-recon reconciliation package export and offline verification

Reviewers can export the complete set of currently-hit impact-import reconciliation entries (the same current-hit receipts the global reconciliation listing serves) as one self-contained package with an offline-recomputable integrity checkpoint, and a third party can verify a received package from its body alone. Both routes are strictly read-only/pure: neither writes any resource, receipt, audit row, or log.

- `GET /v1/impact-recon-package?local_available=...&matches=...` — read-only one-call export of every currently-hit reconciliation entry together with its checkpoint. It accepts exactly the global reconciliation listing's two filters with the same semantics: optional `local_available` and `matches`, each provided at most once and accepting only the lowercase literals `true`/`false` (blank, capitalized, numeric, repeated, or other spellings are `422`), combining as logical AND against the read-time reconciliation. `limit` and `cursor` are not accepted and, like every other undeclared parameter, are `422 validation_error`; the package always covers the entire filtered set in one read. The request carries no body: any body bytes (even whitespace, arbitrary bytes, or malformed JSON) are `422 validation_error`, rejected before any query parameter, receipt, or local impact is read. The success body is compact UTF-8 JSON (compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII) terminated by exactly one newline, strictly `{"checkpoint", "entries"}` in that member order: `checkpoint` is exactly `{"checkpoint_version", "digest_algorithm", "entry_count", "entries_digest_hex"}` with `checkpoint_version="pir-checkpoint-v1"`, `digest_algorithm="sha256"`, the total number of matched entries, and the digest below; `entries` lists, in the receipts' stable creation order (`created_at` with the persistent insertion-order tiebreaker), exactly the views the global reconciliation listing serves for the same effective filter — each item exactly the single-receipt public view (`id`, `checkpoint_version`, `impact_count`, `impacts_digest_hex`, UTC `received_at`) followed by `local_available`, `local_checkpoint` (the four-field unfiltered local revocation-impact checkpoint, identical for every entry), and `matches`; the imported impacts array and every raw signature, payload, content, or evidence byte are never included. `entries_digest_hex` is the SHA-256 hex digest over exactly the `entries` array returned in the same response: the array keeps its element order, every nested object's keys (including `local_checkpoint`'s) are sorted recursively by Unicode code point, and serialization uses compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII, and UTF-8 encoding, so the digest is reproducible by an external verifier from the package body alone; both halves derive from a single read-only state read, so they are always mutually consistent and the returned pair verifies via the stateless verification route below. An empty match set is still a legal snapshot: `"entries": []`, `entry_count: 0`, and the deterministic digest of the empty array; every number renders as an integer (no negative zero or non-finite value). Repeated reads and reads across an app restart return the same package for the same persisted state. The export is strictly read-only — success, empty results, failures, and retries create, modify, or delete no receipt, resource, or audit event — and every existing interface and the existing error JSON are unchanged. Only `GET` is accepted; `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` are rejected with `405 method_not_allowed`.
- `POST /v1/impact-recon-verifications` — stateless offline verification of a received impact-recon package, for third-party verifiers. The request body is exactly `{"checkpoint", "entries"}`: `checkpoint` is exactly `{"checkpoint_version", "digest_algorithm", "entry_count", "entries_digest_hex"}` with `checkpoint_version="pir-checkpoint-v1"`, `digest_algorithm="sha256"`, a non-negative integer `entry_count`, and an `entries_digest_hex` of exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters; `entries` is an array of exactly `entry_count` items, each carrying exactly the exported eight fields with strict types — non-empty strings for `id` and `checkpoint_version`, a non-negative integral `impact_count`, an `impacts_digest_hex` of exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, a strict RFC 3339 UTC `received_at` (`Z` or `+00:00`, seconds required, no naive or non-UTC value), strict JSON booleans `local_available` and `matches`, and a `local_checkpoint` object of exactly its four fields (`checkpoint_version="provenance-revocation-impact-checkpoint-v1"`, `digest_algorithm="sha256"`, a non-negative integer `impact_count`, and a 64-lowercase-hex `impacts_digest_hex`). No undeclared member is accepted on any object, so no raw signature, public key, payload, content, evidence, or imported-impacts field can enter the request; no cross-field association between the flags, the receipt identity, and the embedded local checkpoint is required. The digest is recomputed over `entries` exactly as received (array order preserved, nested object keys sorted recursively by Unicode code point, compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII, UTF-8, SHA-256). A match returns `200` with exactly `{"valid": true}` and no other field; a structurally valid request whose recomputed digest differs returns `200` with exactly `{"valid": false, "computed_digest_hex": ...}` carrying the 64-lowercase-hex recomputed value. Malformed JSON; a missing, extra, null, or wrong-typed top-level or nested field; the wrong package or local version/algorithm; a malformed digest or timestamp; an array whose length differs from `entry_count`; and any undeclared or raw-material field are all `422 validation_error`. The route accepts no query parameters — any parameter is `422 validation_error`. It is purely a function of the request body: it never queries, creates, or modifies any local receipt or other resource, writes no audit row or log, and never resolves any identifier, so unknown resources, repeated identical requests, and differing local state all produce the same verdict. The success body is compact UTF-8 JSON (compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII) terminated by exactly one newline; times stay UTC and every count renders as an integer. Every existing interface and the existing error JSON semantics are unchanged.

## Read-only proof access grants

A read-only access grant authorizes another actor to read one existing attestation through a protected endpoint. Grants are immutable and append-only: there is no update or delete path, and a grant never mutates the attestation it references.

Both protected routes authenticate every request with three headers:

- `X-PA` — the calling actor id;
- `X-PT` — the request timestamp as an RFC 3339 UTC instant (`Z` or an explicit `+00:00`; no naive or non-UTC value), no more than **300 seconds** from the server's current time;
- `X-PS` — a standard-Base64 Ed25519 signature (64 raw bytes) over the exact UTF-8 compact JSON array (compact separators, non-ASCII emitted unescaped):

  ```
  ["provenance-access-v1",method,path,timestamp,body_sha256]
  ```

  `method` is the uppercase HTTP method, `path` is the request path without any query string, `timestamp` is the exact `X-PT` header value, and `body_sha256` is the lowercase-hex SHA-256 of the actual request body bytes — the digest of zero bytes for an empty (GET) body. The signature is accepted if it verifies under **any** public key of a non-revoked attestation created by the calling actor; a revoked attestation's key never authenticates.

- `POST /v1/attestation-access-grants` — JSON body contains exactly `attestation_id` and `grantee_actor_id`; any undeclared field is rejected. Only the attestation's `signer_actor_id` (authenticated as above) may create a grant. The first creation returns `201` with exactly `{id, attestation_id, grantee_actor_id, created_at}` — a stable `aag_` id and a UTC `created_at`. A retried submission for the same `(attestation_id, grantee_actor_id)` pair returns `200` with the original record and writes no new row or audit event; a different grantee forms an independent, immutable record. The first grant write and its `attestation.access_granted` audit event commit in a single transaction. Missing credentials, an unparseable or out-of-window timestamp, malformed signature encoding, a signature no current key of the actor verifies, malformed fields or JSON, a missing attestation, a missing grantee actor, and a caller who is not the attestation's signer are all `422 validation_error`; no failure writes a resource or an audit event.
- `GET /v1/protected/attestations/{attestation_id}` — read-only. Only the attestation's `signer_actor_id` or an actor holding an access grant for that exact attestation may call it; success returns the existing attestation's public view (the same fields as `GET /v1/attestations/{id}`). A missing target, an unauthenticated caller, and an unauthorized caller all return the **same opaque `404 not_found`**, so existence is never revealed to a caller without access. An unparseable/out-of-window timestamp or a signature that is not canonical Base64 of exactly 64 bytes is `422 validation_error`. The read writes no resource and no audit event.
- `GET /v1/attestations/{attestation_id}/access-grants` — read-only, signed with the same `X-PA`/`X-PT`/`X-PS` contract over the empty GET body (the signed path carries no query string). Only the attestation's `signer_actor_id` may call it — a grantee who can read the protected proof cannot list its grants. A missing or unauthenticatable credential, a missing target, and a non-signer all return the **same opaque `404 not_found`**; an unparseable/out-of-window timestamp or a malformed signature is `422 validation_error`. Success is strictly `{"items", "count", "next_cursor"}`; each item carries exactly `{id, attestation_id, grantee_actor_id, created_at}` in stable creation order (`created_at` with the monotonic sequence tiebreaker) and never echoes any revocation, private key, raw signature, authentication header, payload, or byte. Only `limit` and `cursor` are accepted: `limit` is a pure decimal integer in `1..100` (default `50`); any undeclared, repeated, blank/whitespace, or otherwise illegal parameter — and any malformed, unsigned, foreign-family, or non-binding cursor — is `422 validation_error`, checked before the target lookup. The opaque cursor is HMAC-signed and bound to the attestation, the authenticated caller, and the effective limit, so it resumes only the query that minted it; continuation pages repeat and omit nothing, the last page carries `next_cursor: null`, and a position past the tail returns `"items": []` with the same `count`. An attestation without grants returns an empty collection; the route is strictly read-only and leaves the existing grant and protected-read interfaces unchanged.

### Read-only tracking of grant revocations

Reviewers can read the immutable grant-revocation records through two read-only routes. Neither route requires the `X-PA`/`X-PT`/`X-PS` headers, both accept **no query parameters** — any, blank, or repeated parameter is `422 validation_error` validated *before* the resource lookup — and both are strictly read-only: a successful read, an empty result, a missing resource, and a parameter failure create or modify no grant, revocation, other resource, or audit event.

- `GET /v1/attestation-access-grant-revocations/{revocation_id}` — returns one existing revocation's public view, exactly `{id, grant_id, revoker_actor_id, reason, created_at}` with a UTC timestamp. The revocation id is the only lookup key — a grant id or attestation id is never reverse-resolved. An unknown id is an explicit `404 attestation_access_grant_revocation_not_found` carrying the requested `revocation_id` (an unknown id supplied together with a query parameter is the 422, since parameters are checked first). The view carries no private key, raw signature, authentication header, claim payload, content, or evidence byte.
- `GET /v1/attestation-access-grants/{grant_id}/revocations` — returns only that existing grant's revocation records as strictly `{"items", "count"}`, each item the exact five-field public view above, in the records' stable creation order (`created_at` with the monotonic sequence tiebreaker). The grant id is the sole lookup key — records are never resolved through a revoker, reason, attestation, or revocation id. An unknown grant is `422 validation_error` with `details.reason="grant_not_found"` (the same boundary as the revocation write route), never an empty collection and never a reverse lookup; an existing grant that has not been revoked returns `{"items": [], "count": 0}`. Repeated reads are deterministic and the views are unchanged across an app restart.

## Content lineage relations

Relations record how content identities descend from one another: `content_id` is the newer version or derived content, `parent_content_id` is its direct source, and `relation_type` is `version_of` or `derived_from`. Relations are immutable and append-only: there is no update or delete path.

- `POST /v1/content-relations` — create a relation between two existing contents. The first creation returns `201` with the stable `rel_` id, both content ids, the relation type, and a UTC `created_at`; a repeat submission of the same three fields returns `200` with the existing relation and writes no row or audit event. An unknown content on either side is `404 content_not_found`; blank identifiers, an unknown relation type, a self-loop, or an edge that would close a lineage cycle are `422 validation_error` and write nothing.
- `GET /v1/content-relations/{relation_id}` — full public fields, or `404 content_relation_not_found`.
- `GET /v1/content-relations?id=...&content_id=...&parent_content_id=...&relation_type=...&from=...&to=...&limit=...&cursor=...` — global read-only search across the immutable lineage relations. Returns `{"items", "count", "next_cursor"}` where each item reuses the single-relation public view (`id`, `content_id`, `parent_content_id`, `relation_type`, UTC `created_at`). Records are returned in stable creation order (`created_at`, with the persistence insertion order breaking same-instant ties, stable across restarts). Optional `id`, `content_id`, and `parent_content_id` are non-empty, case/whitespace-sensitive exact matches; optional `relation_type` accepts only the literals `version_of` and `derived_from`. Every filter combines as logical AND — an unknown or nonexistent value yields an empty collection, never a 404; `from` and `to` are strict RFC 3339 UTC instants applied as inclusive `created_at` bounds, and `from` must not be later than `to`. `limit` is a pure decimal integer from 1 to 100 defaulting to 50; `cursor` is an opaque HMAC-signed server token (its own `rl1` family) binding to every effective filter and the limit, so pages resume without duplication or omission, `count` is always the filtered total across all pages, the first page carries no cursor, and the final and past-the-tail pages carry `next_cursor: null` with an empty page at or past the tail. Blank, wrong-typed, malformed, out-of-range, repeated, or undeclared parameters; an invalid `relation_type`; a `from` later than `to`; an empty, malformed, tampered, foreign-family, or filter/limit-mismatching `cursor`; and any non-empty request body (whitespace, arbitrary bytes, or bad JSON included) are all `422 validation_error`, validated before any relation record is read and never returning partial results. No matching records yields an empty collection. The request body must be empty. Success, empty results, and failures are strictly read-only: no relation or audit event is created, modified, or deleted; relation creation idempotency, self-loop/cycle rejection, the detail and per-content reads, lineage traversal, and the existing error JSON are unchanged. `PUT`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` on this route are rejected with `405 method_not_allowed`.
- `GET /v1/contents/{content_id}/relations` — the in- and out-edges of one content in stable creation order as `{"items", "count"}`; an unknown content id is `404 content_not_found`.
- `GET /v1/contents/{content_id}/lineage?direction=ancestors|descendants&max_depth=...&relation_type=...&min_depth=...&limit=...&cursor=...` — read-only multi-hop traversal. `direction` is required and must be exactly `ancestors` (content to direct source, following edges onward) or `descendants` (the reverse); `max_depth` is an optional integer from 1 to 32 defaulting to 8. Optional filters and paging: `relation_type` is exactly `version_of` or `derived_from` (absent means no edge-type filtering); `min_depth` is an integer from 1 to 32 defaulting to 1 and must not exceed the effective `max_depth`; `limit` is an integer from 1 to 100 defaulting to 50; `cursor` is an opaque server token returned by a previous page. Filtering only removes returned items — it never prunes traversal reachability, changes shortest-depth dedup, or changes depth/discovery ordering: an item matches `relation_type` when the edge through which it was *first* reached (at its shortest depth) has that type. Missing/blank/illegal `direction`, an empty/non-integer/out-of-range/repeated `max_depth`, `min_depth`, or `limit`, an unknown `relation_type`, a `min_depth` greater than `max_depth`, and an empty, malformed, tampered, expired-format, or query-parameter-mismatching `cursor` are all `422 validation_error` — nothing is defaulted or silently normalized, and no resource or audit row is written. The origin is never included; only contents reachable within the depth limit are returned, each deduplicated at its shortest depth, ordered by depth ascending and within a level by the discovering edge's stable creation order, as `{"items", "count", "next_cursor"}` where each item is the full public content view plus an integer `depth`. `count` is the total number of items after filtering, independent of the page returned; `next_cursor` is an opaque token for the next page or `null` on the final (and only, for an empty result) page. Re-sending a cursor with the same effective parameters resumes exactly where the previous page ended, with no duplicates or omissions; cursors are HMAC-signed and bind to the origin, direction, and every effective filter/limit value. No reachable contents yields an empty set. An unknown origin is `404 content_not_found`. The query reads only contents and relations (no resource or audit writes), deduplicates visited nodes, and terminates even if anomalous history contains a cycle.

The first relation creation and its `content_relation.created` audit event commit in a single transaction.

## Authentication public-key rotation

A subject can rotate the public key that authenticates its protected-route requests without minting a new attestation. A rotation introduces a new Ed25519 public key that immediately joins the subject's **non-revoked authentication set** — the union of the public keys on the subject's existing non-revoked attestations and the subject's active rotation keys. No new attestation or proof is required, and a public key still carried by an existing non-revoked attestation remains valid. The service never receives a private key or a raw signature. Both routes authenticate with the same `X-PA`/`X-PT`/`X-PS` header contract as the other protected routes, and the authenticated caller is always the rotation's subject.

- `POST /v1/authentication-key-rotations` — JSON body contains exactly a non-empty `actor_id` and a standard-Base64 `new_public_key` that decodes to exactly **32 bytes**; any undeclared field is rejected. The caller must authenticate as that same `actor_id`, which must already exist. The first creation returns `201` with exactly `{id, actor_id, new_public_key, active, created_at, retired_at}` — a stable `akr_` id, the subject, the Base64 public key, `active: true`, a timezone-aware UTC `created_at`, and `retired_at: null`. The first write and its `authentication_key.rotated` audit event commit in a single transaction. A retried submission for the same subject and public key returns `200` with the original record and writes no row or audit event — this stays idempotent even after the record has been retired, in which case the original (now retired) record is returned unchanged. A different public key for the same subject forms an independent rotation.
- `POST /v1/authentication-key-rotations/{rotation_id}/retire` — the request body is **empty** (the signed `body_sha256` is therefore the digest of zero bytes). Only the owning subject may retire a record, and only while it is active. Success returns the record with `active: false` and a timezone-aware UTC `retired_at` (the `akr_` id, subject, and public key are unchanged), and the state change and the `authentication_key.retired` audit event commit in a single transaction. The retired key stops authenticating immediately; the record and its `authentication_key.rotated` history are preserved.
- `GET /v1/actors/{actor_id}/authentication-key-rotations` — read-only reviewer retrieval of one existing subject's key-rotation history; no authentication headers are required. It accepts exactly `limit` and `cursor` (any other parameter, and any repeated parameter, is `422 validation_error` before the subject lookup). Success returns strictly `{"items", "count", "next_cursor"}`; each item is exactly the existing public rotation view `{id, actor_id, new_public_key, active, created_at, retired_at}` — no private key, raw signature, authentication header, or internal ordering surrogate is ever present — and records follow stable creation order (`created_at` with the monotonic sequence tiebreaker), active and retired records together. `limit` is a pure decimal integer from 1 to 100 defaulting to 50; `cursor` is an opaque HMAC-signed server token in its own family, bound to the path subject and the effective limit, so pages resume without duplication or omission, `count` is always the subject's rotation total on every page (including a page at or past the tail, which returns empty `items`, the original `count`, and `next_cursor: null`), and the final page carries `next_cursor: null`. Blank, non-integer, out-of-range, signed, decimal, or padded `limit` values; blank, malformed, tampered, wrongly-signed, expired-format, wrong-claim-set, cross-endpoint, or subject/limit-mismatching `cursor` values are all `422 validation_error` — nothing is silently normalized. An existing subject without rotations is an empty collection (`count` 0); an unknown subject is `404 unknown_actor`, decided only after query validation. The read writes no resource and no audit event.

An active rotation key authenticates `POST /v1/attestation-access-grants`, `GET /v1/protected/attestations/{attestation_id}`, `GET /v1/attestations/{attestation_id}/access-grants`, and the two rotation routes exactly as an attestation key would; retiring it removes it from the set at once. The request body and the credentials are validated before any state change. An unknown subject, an unknown rotation id, a caller who is not the record's subject, and a repeat retirement of an already-retired record are all `422 validation_error` (existence is never revealed to a non-owner) and write neither a resource nor an audit event; credential failures use the same `validation_error` code as on the grant route.

## Subject trust policies and authorization decisions

A subject can register one immutable trust policy — the number of distinct qualified signers it requires before a claim or evidence bundle is trusted — and then ask the service for authorization decisions computed under that policy. A policy is append-only and immutable: there is deliberately no update, delete, deactivate, or replace path (any such attempt is `405 method_not_allowed`). Both routes authenticate with the same `X-PA`/`X-PT`/`X-PS` header contract as the other protected routes, and both answer with compact UTF-8 JSON terminated by exactly one newline, with all numbers rendered as integers (never negative zero or a non-finite value).

- `POST /v1/trust-policies` — JSON body contains exactly a non-empty `actor_id` and a `threshold`; any undeclared field is rejected. `threshold` is a pure decimal integer from 1 to 100: booleans, strings, and fractional or exponent-notation numbers are `422 validation_error`, never coerced. The caller must authenticate as that same `actor_id`, which must already exist: an unknown subject and a caller/subject mismatch are both `422 validation_error` and write nothing. The first registration returns `201` with exactly `{id, actor_id, threshold, enabled, created_at}` — a stable `atp_` id, the subject, the threshold, `enabled: true`, and a timezone-aware UTC `created_at` — and the policy row and its `actor_trust_policy.created` audit event commit in a single transaction. Each subject has at most one policy: a retried registration of the same subject and threshold returns `200` with the original policy and writes no new row, audit event, or identifier, while the same subject with a different threshold is `409 actor_trust_policy_conflict` and likewise writes nothing. Missing credentials, an unparseable or out-of-window timestamp, malformed signature encoding, a signature no current key of the actor verifies, malformed fields, and malformed JSON are all `422 validation_error`; no failure writes a resource or an audit event.
- `GET /v1/trust-policies?actor_id=...&limit=...&cursor=...` — read-only retrieval of the existing immutable trust policies; no authentication headers are required. The request body must be empty: carrying any bytes (even whitespace or malformed JSON) is `422 validation_error`, rejected before any parameter or policy is read. The success body is compact UTF-8 JSON terminated by exactly one newline, with members in exactly the order `items`, `count`, `next_cursor`; each item is the existing policy public view (`id`, `actor_id`, `threshold`, `enabled`, UTC `created_at`) in the policies' stable creation order (`created_at` with the monotonic `seq` tiebreaker). Optional `actor_id` is a non-empty, case/whitespace-sensitive exact match on the policy subject (absent means unfiltered) and is never resolved for existence — an unknown subject is an empty collection, not a 404. `count` is the filtered total covering every page, independent of the page returned. `limit` is a pure decimal integer from 1 to 100 defaulting to 50; `cursor` is an opaque HMAC-signed server token (its own `tp1` family) bound to the effective `actor_id` (`null` when unfiltered) and the effective limit, so pages resume without duplication or omission and the final page carries `next_cursor: null` (a cursor at or past the tail returns an empty page with the original `count`). Blank/illegal/repeated/undeclared parameters and an empty, whitespace-only, malformed, tampered, cross-endpoint/foreign-family, or filter/limit-mismatching `cursor` are all `422 validation_error` — nothing is silently defaulted or normalized. No match returns `{"items": [], "count": 0, "next_cursor": null}`. The retrieval is strictly read-only: success, empty results, repeated reads, and failures create no policy, resource, or audit event, and the view never carries a private key, raw signature, claim payload, content, or evidence bytes.
- `GET /v1/trust-decisions?target_type=claim|evidence_bundle&target_id=...` — read-only authorization decision under the **calling subject's current policy** (no other subject's policy ever participates). The request carries no body: any body bytes at all (even whitespace or malformed JSON) are `422 validation_error`, checked before the parameters. `target_type` is required and must be exactly `claim` or `evidence_bundle`; `target_id` is required and non-blank; any undeclared, repeated, blank, or illegal parameter is `422 validation_error`, validated before authentication. Missing or unauthenticatable credentials return the same opaque `404 not_found` as the other protected read routes (existence is never revealed); an unparseable/out-of-window timestamp or a malformed signature encoding is `422 validation_error`. When the caller has **no policy**, the target is never looked up — its existence is neither checked nor revealed — and the response is `200` with `{"target_type", "target_id", "policy_id": null, "threshold": null, "qualified_signer_count": 0, "decision": "untrusted", "reason": "policy_missing"}`. With a policy, the target must exist: an unknown target is `404 claim_not_found` or `404 evidence_bundle_not_found` according to the declared `target_type` (claim and evidence-bundle ids never cross-match), never a partial decision. Otherwise the response is `200` with the echoed `target_type`/`target_id`, the deciding `policy_id` and `threshold`, the `qualified_signer_count` (verified, non-revoked attestations of the exact target, deduplicated by signing actor — the same counting as the trust-evaluation route), and the `decision`/`reason` pair: `trusted`/`threshold_met` when the count reaches the policy threshold, `untrusted`/`below_threshold` otherwise. The decision is computed live on every request and is strictly read-only: decisions, no-policy responses, missing targets, and failed requests write no resource and no audit event.

## Audit-event search

Compliance auditors can search the append-only audit trail directly. The endpoint is strictly read-only: it never creates, updates, or deletes any resource or audit row, on success or on failure.

- `GET /v1/audit-events?event_type=...&resource_id=...&from=...&to=...&limit=...&cursor=...` — read-only search over the existing audit events. Returns `{"items", "count", "next_cursor"}` where each item carries exactly `event_type`, `resource_id`, and a timezone-aware UTC `created_at`, ordered by the events' stable creation order. Optional `event_type` and `resource_id` are non-empty, case/whitespace-sensitive exact matches that combine as logical AND; `from` and `to` are strict RFC 3339 UTC instants (e.g. `2026-01-02T12:30:00Z` or `...+00:00`) applied as inclusive `created_at` bounds, and `from` must not be later than `to`. `limit` is an integer from 1 to 100 defaulting to 50; `cursor` is an opaque HMAC-signed server token that binds to every effective filter and the limit, so pages resume without duplication or omission, `count` is always the filtered total, and the final page carries `next_cursor: null`. Blank/illegal/repeated/undeclared parameters, a `from` later than `to`, and a blank, malformed, tampered, foreign-family, or filter-mismatching `cursor` are all `422 validation_error` — nothing is silently defaulted or normalized. No matching events yields an empty collection. The query writes no resource or audit rows, and neither does any rejected request.
- `GET /v1/audit-events/checkpoint/package` — read-only one-call export, for an external compliance system, of a filtered audit-event sequence together with its integrity checkpoint. It accepts exactly the four checkpoint filters `event_type`, `resource_id`, `from`, and `to` with the exact-match, strict RFC 3339 UTC, repeated-parameter, and undeclared-parameter semantics of the checkpoint route; `limit` and `cursor` are not accepted, and blank/illegal/repeated/undeclared parameters and a `from` later than `to` are all `422 validation_error`, validated before any event is read. The success body is strictly `{"checkpoint", "events"}`: `checkpoint` is exactly the four-field body of the existing `GET /v1/audit-events/checkpoint` route for the same effective filter (`checkpoint_version="provenance-audit-checkpoint-v1"`, `digest_algorithm="sha256"`, `event_count`, `events_digest_hex`), and `events` lists, in stable creation order, the existing audit-event public views matched by that same filter — each item exactly `{"event_type", "resource_id", "created_at"}` with a timezone-aware UTC timestamp. The checkpoint digest is computed over exactly the `events` array returned in the same response under the existing checkpoint canonical rules (array order kept, object keys sorted by Unicode code point, compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII, UTF-8, SHA-256), and both halves derive from a single read-only state read, so they are always mutually consistent; the returned pair verifies offline via the stateless checkpoint-verification route. An empty match set returns `"events": []` with `event_count: 0` and the digest of the empty array. The route is strictly read-only: success, empty results, and failures create, modify, or delete no resource and add no audit event; repeated reads and reads across an app restart return the same package, and the existing audit-event search, checkpoint, verification, checkpoint-import receipts, identifiers, UTC fields, and error JSON are unchanged.
- `POST /v1/audit-events/checkpoint-imports` — controlled registration, for an external compliance system, of an audit checkpoint that was already received and verified offline. The request body is exactly `{"checkpoint", "events"}`, with the field structure, fixed version/algorithm, event count, strict RFC 3339 UTC timestamps, and canonical digest rules of the stateless checkpoint-verification route: `checkpoint` is exactly `{"checkpoint_version", "digest_algorithm", "event_count", "events_digest_hex"}` with `checkpoint_version="provenance-audit-checkpoint-v1"`, `digest_algorithm="sha256"`, a non-negative integer `event_count`, and a 64-lowercase-hex `events_digest_hex`; `events` is an array of exactly `event_count` items, each exactly `{"event_type", "resource_id", "created_at"}` with non-empty strings and a strict RFC 3339 UTC timestamp. The digest is recomputed over the events exactly as received (array order preserved, object keys sorted by Unicode code point, compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII, UTF-8, SHA-256). Verification is decided by the request body alone: the events described by the checkpoint are never created, modified, or queried against local state, so whether they exist locally cannot change the receipt, and no such event is materialized. Missing or extra top-level or nested fields, wrong member types, the wrong version/algorithm, a malformed digest or timestamp, an event array whose length differs from `event_count`, malformed JSON, and a digest mismatch are all `422 validation_error` and write nothing — a mismatch carries `details.reason="events_digest_mismatch"` and the `computed_digest_hex`. On success the receiving identity is exactly `(checkpoint_version, event_count, events_digest_hex)`; the first submission returns `201` with a stable deterministic `aci_` receipt id, the three identity fields, and a UTC `received_at`, and writes the receipt row together with the `audit.checkpoint_imported` audit event in a single transaction. A retry for the same identity returns `200` with the original receipt (including its original `received_at`) and writes no second row or audit event — even when the retried events themselves no longer match, in which case the retry is `422` and the original record is untouched. The full event array and all raw event data are never copied or persisted: the receipt holds only the identity fields.
- `GET /v1/audit-events/checkpoint-imports/{import_id}` — read the public receipt for one registered checkpoint import: exactly `{"id", "checkpoint_version", "events_digest_hex", "event_count", "received_at"}`, with `received_at` a UTC timestamp. The event array and every raw event datum are never returned. An unknown id is an explicit `404 audit_checkpoint_import_not_found` carrying the requested `import_id`; the read is strictly read-only and writes no resource or audit event.
- `GET /v1/audit-events/checkpoint-imports/{import_id}/reconciliation` — read-only reconciliation, for an external compliance reviewer, of one registered checkpoint-import receipt against the current local audit sequence. The route accepts no query parameters — any parameter or repeated parameter is `422 validation_error`, validated before the receipt lookup — and an unknown id is the existing `404 audit_checkpoint_import_not_found` carrying the requested `import_id`. The success body is strictly `{"import_id", "local_checkpoint", "matches"}`: `import_id` is the receipt id; `local_checkpoint` is the four-field checkpoint (`checkpoint_version="provenance-audit-checkpoint-v1"`, `digest_algorithm="sha256"`, `event_count`, `events_digest_hex`) computed over the complete, unfiltered local audit-event sequence under exactly the existing `GET /v1/audit-events/checkpoint` rules — same fixed version and algorithm, stable creation order, UTC representation, and canonical SHA-256 digest semantics (an empty local sequence yields `event_count: 0` and the digest of the empty array). `matches` is `true` only when the receipt's `checkpoint_version`, `event_count`, and `events_digest_hex` all equal the corresponding local checkpoint fields; any difference (including a local sequence that has since grown or changed) is `false`, with the current checkpoint still reported. The imported event array is never read (it is not persisted) or echoed, and the verdict is never inferred from any unpersisted material. Success, an empty local trail, parameter failures, and a missing receipt are all strictly read-only: no resource, receipt, or audit event is created or modified, and the existing checkpoint, import receipt, audit-event search, identifiers, UTC fields, and error JSON are unchanged.
- `GET /v1/audit-events/checkpoint-import-reconciliations?limit=...&cursor=...` — read-only, paginated reconciliation of every existing checkpoint-import receipt against the current local audit sequence. Only `limit` and `cursor` are accepted: any undeclared, repeated, blank, or illegal parameter is `422 validation_error`. The success body is strictly `{"items", "count", "next_cursor"}`; receipts are returned in the same stable creation order (`created_at` with the monotonic `seq` tiebreaker) and `count` is the total number of receipts, independent of the page. Each item is the existing single-receipt public view (`id`, `checkpoint_version`, `events_digest_hex`, `event_count`, UTC `received_at`) plus `local_checkpoint` and `matches`; `local_checkpoint` is the four-field checkpoint computed over the complete, unfiltered local audit sequence under exactly the existing `GET /v1/audit-events/checkpoint` rules, and `matches` is `true` only when the receipt's version, event count, and digest all equal that checkpoint — agreeing item-for-item with the single-receipt reconciliation route. `limit` is a pure decimal integer from 1 to 100 defaulting to 50; `cursor` is an opaque HMAC-signed server token (its own `cr1` family) binding to the effective limit, so pages resume without duplication or omission and the final page carries `next_cursor: null` (a cursor at or past the end returns empty `items`, the total `count`, and `null`; an empty, malformed, tampered, foreign-family, or limit-mismatching cursor is `422 validation_error`). No receipts is an empty collection (`{"items": [], "count": 0, "next_cursor": null}`). The imported event arrays are never read or echoed; the route is strictly read-only and writes no resource, receipt, or audit event, and it is compatible with the existing single-receipt reconciliation, checkpoint, receipt search, and error JSON.

Errors are distinct JSON bodies under `{"error": {"code", ...}}`: `actor_already_exists` (409), `unknown_actor` (404), `content_not_found` (404), `claim_not_found` (404), `evidence_bundle_not_found` (404), `attestation_not_found` (404), `attestation_revocation_not_found` (404), `attestation_access_grant_revocation_not_found` (404), `content_relation_not_found` (404), `content_export_job_not_found` (404), `content_export_request_conflict` (409), `actor_trust_policy_conflict` (409), `attestation_verification_failed` (422), and `validation_error` (422); the protected attestation read answers a missing target, an unauthenticated caller, and an unauthorized caller with one opaque `not_found` (404); a content export job that is not pending when run returns `conflict` (409), and a failed run records `content_export_failed` in the job's `error` field (the run itself returns `200`). Every successful actor, content, claim, evidence bundle, attestation, attestation revocation, attestation access grant, content relation, authentication key rotation, and actor trust policy creation appends one audit row (`event_type`, `resource_id`, UTC `created_at`) in the same transaction as the resource write; a revocation records the `attestation.revoked` event, an access grant records the `attestation.access_granted` event, a rotation records the `authentication_key.rotated` event, retiring a rotation records the `authentication_key.retired` event, a content export job creation records the `content_export_job.created` event, running an export job records the `content_export_job.run` event, and a trust policy registration records the `actor_trust_policy.created` event. All returned timestamps are timezone-aware UTC.

## Tests

```bash
pip install -e ".[test]"   # or: pip install -r requirements.lock
pytest
```

Tests are deterministic and fully offline (in-memory and temporary-file SQLite, no network).

"""Deterministic canonical JSON for claim payload and exchange-manifest digests.

A claim commits to its payload through a SHA-256 digest of a canonical
serialization, so the digest is stable across key orderings, insignificant
whitespace, and Unicode escaping choices. The exchange manifest uses the
same canonical form for its bundle snapshot. The raw payload itself is
never persisted or echoed back.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
from typing import Any

CANONICAL_DIGEST_ALGORITHM = "sha256"


def canonical_json_bytes(value: Any) -> bytes:
    """Serialize ``value`` deterministically: sorted keys, minimal separators.

    ``ensure_ascii=False`` plus UTF-8 encoding keeps the canonical form
    independent of how the input escaped non-ASCII characters.
    """
    return json.dumps(
        value,
        sort_keys=True,
        separators=(",", ":"),
        ensure_ascii=False,
        allow_nan=False,
    ).encode("utf-8")


def payload_digest_hex(payload: Any) -> str:
    """Return the SHA-256 hex digest of the canonical claim payload bytes."""
    return hashlib.sha256(canonical_json_bytes(payload)).hexdigest()


def _ordered_root_canonical_bytes(value: Any) -> bytes:
    """Serialize with the root member order kept and nested keys sorted.

    The root object keeps its member names in the received order and arrays
    keep their element order; every nested object's members are sorted by
    Unicode code point. Serialization is otherwise identical to
    :func:`canonical_json_bytes` (compact separators, non-ASCII emitted
    unescaped, UTF-8 encoded), so the bytes are reproducible by an external
    verifier from the received JSON alone.
    """

    def canonicalize(value: Any, *, sort_root: bool) -> Any:
        if isinstance(value, dict):
            items = sorted(value.items()) if sort_root else value.items()
            # Every nested object is sorted; the root alone keeps its order.
            return {key: canonicalize(member, sort_root=True) for key, member in items}
        if isinstance(value, list):
            return [canonicalize(item, sort_root=True) for item in value]
        return value

    normalized = canonicalize(value, sort_root=False)
    return json.dumps(
        normalized,
        separators=(",", ":"),
        ensure_ascii=False,
        allow_nan=False,
    ).encode("utf-8")


def canonical_exchange_snapshot_bytes(snapshot: Any) -> bytes:
    """Serialize an exchange snapshot under the manifest canonical rules.

    Unlike :func:`canonical_json_bytes`, the snapshot root keeps its member

    record,
    local_available: bool,
    local_checkpoint: RevocationImpactCheckpointResponse,
    matches: bool,
) -> ImpactReconEntryResponse:
    # Exactly the existing global-reconciliation list item: the receipt
    # public view with the local availability flag, current local
    # checkpoint, and match verdict; the imported impacts array is absent.
    return ImpactReconEntryResponse(
        id=record.id,
        checkpoint_version=record.checkpoint_version,
        impact_count=record.impact_count,
        impacts_digest_hex=record.impacts_digest_hex,
        received_at=record.created_at,
        local_available=local_available,
        local_checkpoint=local_checkpoint,
        matches=matches,
    )


@router.get("/impact-recon-package")
async def export_impact_recon_package(
    request: Request, session: DbSession
) -> Response:
    # Read-only export of every currently-hit impact-import reconciliation
    # entry together with an offline-recomputable checkpoint. The GET
    # request body must be empty: carrying any bytes (even whitespace,
    # arbitrary bytes, or malformed JSON) is a 422 validated before any
    # query parameter, receipt, or local impact is read.
    raw_body = await request.body()
    if raw_body:
        raise _query_validation_error(
            "body",
            "request body must be empty",
            "value_error.body",
        )

    # The filter contract is exactly the global reconciliation listing's
    # minus pagination: only local_available/matches are accepted, so
    # limit/cursor and every other undeclared parameter are rejected rather
    # than ignored, a repeated scalar is rejected instead of silently
    # taking the last value, and only the lowercase literals true/false
    # are accepted.
    raw = request.query_params

    unknown = set(raw) - _IMPACT_RECON_PACKAGE_PARAMS
    if unknown:
        # A typo or a pagination parameter never silently changes the
        # snapshot.
        field = sorted(unknown)[0]
        raise _query_validation_error(
            field, f"unknown query parameter: {field}", "value_error.unknown"
        )

    local_available_filter = _parse_bool_literal_param(raw, "local_available")
    matches_filter = _parse_bool_literal_param(raw, "matches")

    # Strictly read-only, and the package derives from one state read under
    # exactly the global reconciliation rules: receipts follow stable
    # creation order, the current local impact set is read once complete
    # and unfiltered (identical for every entry), and the two filters apply
    # to the read-time reconciliation and combine as logical AND. No
    # resource, receipt, or audit event is written; an empty match set
    # yields "entries": [] with entry_count 0 and the digest of the empty
    # array.
    records = service.list_revocation_impact_import_reconciliations(session)
    local_checkpoint = _local_revocation_impact_checkpoint(session)
    available = local_checkpoint.impact_count > 0

    entry_views: list[ImpactReconEntryResponse] = []
    for record in records:
        record_matches = (
            record.checkpoint_version == local_checkpoint.checkpoint_version
            and record.impact_count == local_checkpoint.impact_count
            and record.impacts_digest_hex == local_checkpoint.impacts_digest_hex
        )
        if (
            local_available_filter is not None
            and available != local_available_filter
        ):
            continue
        if matches_filter is not None and record_matches != matches_filter:
            continue
        entry_views.append(
            _impact_recon_package_item(
                record, available, local_checkpoint, record_matches
            )
        )

    # mode="json" yields exactly the wire view served in this response's
    # entries member (UTC datetimes as RFC 3339 strings), so the
    # checkpoint binds to exactly those entries and is reproducible by an
    # external verifier from the package body alone.
    entry_payloads = [view.model_dump(mode="json") for view in entry_views]
    package = ImpactReconPackageResponse(
        checkpoint=ImpactReconCheckpointResponse(
            checkpoint_version=IMPACT_RECON_CHECKPOINT_VERSION,
            digest_algorithm=IMPACT_RECON_DIGEST_ALGORITHM,
            entry_count=len(entry_payloads),
            entries_digest_hex=canonical.impact_recon_entries_digest_hex(
                entry_payloads
            ),
        ),
        entries=entry_views,
    )
    # Compact UTF-8 JSON, null/boolean literals, integral numbers only
    # (never a negative zero or non-finite number), terminated by exactly
    # one newline; root members appear as checkpoint, entries.
    body = (
        json.dumps(
            package.model_dump(mode="json"),
            separators=(",", ":"),
            ensure_ascii=False,
            allow_nan=False,
        )
        + "\n"
    ).encode("utf-8")
    return Response(content=body, media_type="application/json")


@router.post(
    "/impact-recon-verifications",
    response_model=ImpactReconVerificationResponse,
    response_model_exclude_none=True,
)
async def verify_impact_recon_package(
    payload: ImpactReconVerificationCreate, request: Request
) -> Response:
    # The route accepts no query parameters: any (or repeated) parameter is
    # a 422 validation_error.
    _reject_any_query_param(request)
    # Strictly stateless: no session is injected, so nothing is queried,
    # created, or modified, and no resource, audit row, or log is written.
    # Verification uses the request body alone; no receipt, impact,
    # attestation, actor, content, or bundle id is ever resolved against
    # local state, so unknown resources, repeated requests, and differing
    # local state verify identically. Malformed JSON and every
    # structural, field, type, count, or digest-format failure are
    # rejected by the request model as a 422 before this body runs.
    body = await request.json()
    # The digest commits to the entries array exactly as received: the raw
    # JSON values (array order, timestamp spellings), not any parsed or
    # re-serialized form. The array keeps its order; nested object keys
    # (including local_checkpoint's) sort by Unicode code point under the
    # checkpoint canonical rules.
    computed_digest_hex = canonical.impact_recon_entries_digest_hex(
        body["entries"]
    )
    if computed_digest_hex == payload.checkpoint.entries_digest_hex:
        result = {"valid": True}
    else:
        result = {
            "valid": False,
            "computed_digest_hex": computed_digest_hex,
        }
    # Compact UTF-8 JSON, boolean literals, terminated by exactly one
    # newline; a match carries no field besides valid.
    data = (
        json.dumps(
            result,
            separators=(",", ":"),
            ensure_ascii=False,
            allow_nan=False,
        )
        + "\n"
    ).encode("utf-8")
    return Response(content=data, media_type="application/json")


_TRUST_EVALUATION_PARAMS = frozenset(
    {"target_type", "target_id", "min_signers"}
)


async def _authenticate_protected(
    request: Request, session: Session, body: bytes, *, read: bool
) -> str:
    """Authenticate an X-PA/X-PT/X-PS protected request.

    On the write route every authentication failure is a ``422``. On the
    read route only malformed credentials are ``422``; a missing or
    unverifiable identity collapses into the same opaque ``404`` as a
    missing target or an unauthorized caller.
    """
    try:
        return access_signing.authenticate(session, request, body)
    except AccessAuthError as exc:
        if read and not exc.malformed:
            raise ProtectedResourceNotFoundError() from exc

import json

    content_id: str,
    actor_id: str,
    claim_type: str,
    payload_digest_hex: str,

    """Return a stable ``clm_``-prefixed identifier for a claim identity.

    The material is a canonical JSON array so fields containing separators

    """Return a stable ``evb_``-prefixed identifier for an evidence identity.

    As with claims, the material is a canonical JSON array so fields
    containing separators cannot collide with different field splits.
    """

        [
            "evidence_bundle",
            claim_id,
            evidence_type,
            digest_algorithm,
            digest_hex,
        ],
        separators=(",", ":"),
        ensure_ascii=False,
    ).encode("utf-8")

            grant_id,
            revoker_actor_id,

        ensure_ascii=False,

            manifest_version,

            manifest_digest_hex,

            checkpoint_version,
            event_count,
            events_digest_hex,
        ],
        separators=(",", ":"),
        ensure_ascii=False,
    ).encode("utf-8")

    impact_count: int,
    impacts_digest_hex: str,

    The identity is exactly the receiving identity: the fixed checkpoint
    version, the claimed impact count, and the impacts SHA-256 digest. The
    impacts array itself never enters the material -- only its verified
    digest -- so the same offline-verified checkpoint always maps to the

    is a canonical JSON array so fields containing separators cannot

    """
    material = json.dumps(
        [
            "revocation_impact_import",
            checkpoint_version,
            impact_count,
            impacts_digest_hex,
        ],
        separators=(",", ":"),
        ensure_ascii=False,
    ).encode("utf-8")
    return "rii_" + hashlib.sha256(material).hexdigest()

    """Return a stable ``cxj_``-prefixed id for a content export job.

    client-supplied request id. A retry of the same pair maps to the same
    job; the same request id for different content maps to a different job
    (and is rejected as a conflict). The material is a canonical JSON array
    so fields containing separators cannot collide with different field
    splits.
    """
    material = json.dumps(
        ["content_export_job", content_id, request_id],
        separators=(",", ":"),
        ensure_ascii=False,

    belongs to (each subject has at most one immutable policy, so a retried
    registration maps to the same record and id). The material is a
    canonical JSON array so fields containing separators cannot collide

    material = json.dumps(
        ["actor_trust_policy", actor_id],
        separators=(",", ":"),
        ensure_ascii=False,
    ).encode("utf-8")

"""Attestation signing contract: the exact bytes a signer commits to.

An attestation proves that an existing signing actor endorses an existing
claim or evidence bundle. The signed message is a UTF-8 JSON array with
compact separators and non-ASCII characters left unescaped, so the bytes are
identical regardless of which language or client produced the signature::

    ["provenance-attestation-v1", target_type, target_id, signer_actor_id]

Only Ed25519 signatures over these exact bytes are accepted; see
:mod:`provenance.ed25519`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json

#: Domain-separation prefix and protocol version of the signed array.
ATTESTATION_MESSAGE_PREFIX = "provenance-attestation-v1"

#: Attestable target types, matched verbatim in the signed message.
TARGET_CLAIM = "claim"
TARGET_EVIDENCE_BUNDLE = "evidence_bundle"
ATTESTATION_TARGET_TYPES = frozenset({TARGET_CLAIM, TARGET_EVIDENCE_BUNDLE})


def attestation_message_bytes(
    target_type: str, target_id: str, signer_actor_id: str
) -> bytes:
    """Return the exact canonical bytes the signer's signature is over."""
    return json.dumps(
        [ATTESTATION_MESSAGE_PREFIX, target_type, target_id, signer_actor_id],
        separators=(",", ":"),
        ensure_ascii=False,
    ).encode("utf-8")

"""Minimal Ed25519 signature verification (RFC 8032), standard library only.

Only :func:`verify` is provided: attestations are self-contained proofs, so
the service never holds or generates private keys. Point arithmetic uses
extended twisted-Edwards coordinates so a verification needs no per-step
modular inversion; there is no third-party dependency, keeping verification
deterministic and fully offline.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib

#: Valid Ed25519 public key length.
PUBLIC_KEY_LENGTH = 32
#: Valid Ed25519 signature length.
SIGNATURE_LENGTH = 64

#: Prime of the base field.
Q = 2**255 - 19
#: Order of the prime-order subgroup (and of the standard base point).
L = 2**252 + 27742317777372353535851937790883648493

#: Curve constant ``d`` and the quartic root of -1 used for x recovery.
D = -121665 * pow(121666, Q - 2, Q) % Q
_D2 = D * 2 % Q
_I = pow(2, (Q - 1) // 4, Q)


class _InvalidPoint(ValueError):
    """Raised when 32 bytes do not encode a valid curve point."""


def _xrecover(y: int) -> int:
    """Recover the even-parity x coordinate from y (RFC 8032 §5.1.3).

    ``x`` satisfies ``x^2 = (y^2 - 1) / (d*y^2 + 1)``.
    """
    u = y * y - 1
    v = D * y * y + 1
    xx = u * pow(v, Q - 2, Q) % Q
    x = pow(xx, (Q + 3) // 8, Q)
    if (x * x - xx) % Q != 0:
        x = x * _I % Q
    if (x * x - xx) % Q != 0:
        raise _InvalidPoint("no square root for x")
    if x & 1:
        x = Q - x
    return x


def _decompress(encoded: bytes) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
    """Decode 32 bytes to extended coordinates ``(X, Y, Z, T)``."""
    if len(encoded) != PUBLIC_KEY_LENGTH:
        raise _InvalidPoint("bad point length")
    y = int.from_bytes(encoded, "little")
    sign = y >> 255
    y &= (1 << 255) - 1
    if y >= Q:
        raise _InvalidPoint("y out of field")
    x = _xrecover(y)
    if (x & 1) != sign:
        x = Q - x
    if (-x * x + y * y - 1 - D * x * x * y * y) % Q != 0:
        raise _InvalidPoint("point not on curve")
    return x, y, 1, x * y % Q


def _add(
    p: tuple[int, int, int, int], q: tuple[int, int, int, int]
) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
    """Extended-coordinate twisted-Edwards addition (add ``d`` = -1)."""
    x1, y1, z1, t1 = p
    x2, y2, z2, t2 = q
    a = (y1 - x1) * (y2 - x2) % Q
    b = (y1 + x1) * (y2 + x2) % Q
    c = t1 * _D2 * t2 % Q
    dd = z1 * 2 * z2 % Q
    e = b - a
    f = dd - c
    g = dd + c
    h = b + a
    return e * f % Q, g * h % Q, f * g % Q, e * h % Q


def _double(
    p: tuple[int, int, int, int]
) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
    """Extended-coordinate doubling."""
    x1, y1, z1, _ = p
    a = x1 * x1 % Q
    b = y1 * y1 % Q
    c = 2 * z1 * z1 % Q
    h = a + b
    e = h - (x1 + y1) * (x1 + y1) % Q
    g = a - b
    f = c + g
    return e * f % Q, g * h % Q, f * g % Q, e * h % Q


def _scalarmult(
    point: tuple[int, int, int, int], scalar: int
) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
    """Scalar multiplication via double-and-add."""
    result = (0, 1, 1, 0)
    addend = point
    while scalar:
        if scalar & 1:
            result = _add(result, addend)
        addend = _double(addend)
        scalar >>= 1
    return result


def _is_identity(p: tuple[int, int, int, int]) -> bool:
    x, y, z, _ = p
    return x % Q == 0 and (y - z) % Q == 0


def _points_equal(
    p: tuple[int, int, int, int], q: tuple[int, int, int, int]
) -> bool:
    # Equality in extended coordinates: X1*Z2 == X2*Z1 and Y1*Z2 == Y2*Z1.
    x1, y1, z1, _ = p
    x2, y2, z2, _ = q
    return (
        (x1 * z2 - x2 * z1) % Q == 0
        and (y1 * z2 - y2 * z1) % Q == 0
    )


#: Standard Ed25519 base point (has prime order L).
B = _decompress(
    bytes.fromhex(
        "5866666666666666666666666666666666666666666666666666666666666666"
    )
)


def _encode_point(p: tuple[int, int, int, int]) -> bytes:
    """Encode an extended point in the compressed 32-byte form.

    Used by tests to construct offline signatures; production verification
    never encodes points.
    """
    x, y, z, _ = p
    zi = pow(z, Q - 2, Q)
    x = x * zi % Q
    y = y * zi % Q
    encoded = y | ((x & 1) << 255)
    return encoded.to_bytes(PUBLIC_KEY_LENGTH, "little")


def verify(public_key: bytes, message: bytes, signature: bytes) -> bool:
    """Verify an Ed25519 signature, returning ``True`` only when valid.

    :param public_key: exactly 32 raw bytes (caller must have length-checked).
    :param message: the exact signed bytes.
    :param signature: exactly 64 raw bytes (caller must have length-checked).

    Decoding follows RFC 8032 strictly: encodings off the curve, non-canonical
    scalars (``S >= L``), and low-order public keys are rejected.
    """
    if len(public_key) != PUBLIC_KEY_LENGTH or len(signature) != SIGNATURE_LENGTH:
        return False
    try:
        a = _decompress(public_key)
        r_point = _decompress(signature[:PUBLIC_KEY_LENGTH])
    except _InvalidPoint:
        return False

    s = int.from_bytes(signature[PUBLIC_KEY_LENGTH:], "little")
    if s >= L:
        return False

    # A valid key lies in the prime-order subgroup: [L]A must be the
    # identity. This rejects all small-subgroup points except the identity,
    # which is rejected explicitly (it would make signatures forgeable).
    if _is_identity(a) or not _is_identity(_scalarmult(a, L)):
        return False

    k = int.from_bytes(
        hashlib.sha512(
            signature[:PUBLIC_KEY_LENGTH] + public_key + message
        ).digest(),
        "little",
    )
    # [S]B == R + [k]A
    return _points_equal(
        _scalarmult(B, s),
        _add(r_point, _scalarmult(a, k)),
    )

def _exchange_import_identity_select(
    manifest_version: str, evidence_bundle_id: str, manifest_digest_hex: str
):
    return select(ExchangeImportRecord).where(
        ExchangeImportRecord.manifest_version == manifest_version,
        ExchangeImportRecord.evidence_bundle_id == evidence_bundle_id,
        ExchangeImportRecord.manifest_digest_hex == manifest_digest_hex,
    )


def create_evidence_bundle_exchange_import(
    session: Session,
    payload: EvidenceBundleExchangeImportCreate,
) -> tuple[ExchangeImportRecord, bool]:
    """Register one offline-verified exchange package, returning ``(record, created)``.

    The caller has already verified the package: the request parses under
    the existing exchange manifest and snapshot structures, its internal
    associations are consistent, and the manifest digest matches the
    canonical SHA-256 of the snapshot exactly as received. This function
    performs no such verification and no local-resource lookup: the bundle
    id in the manifest is an opaque reference, so whether the referenced
    resources exist locally never changes the outcome.

    The receiving identity is ``(manifest_version, evidence_bundle_id,
    manifest_digest_hex)``; the snapshot itself is never stored. A first
    submission writes the receipt row and its
    ``evidence_bundle.exchange_imported`` audit event in a single
    transaction. A retried submission for the same identity returns the
    existing record with ``created=False`` and writes nothing -- no second
    row and no second audit event.
    """
    manifest = payload.manifest
    manifest_version = manifest.manifest_version
    evidence_bundle_id = manifest.evidence_bundle_id
    manifest_digest_hex = manifest.manifest_digest_hex

    existing = session.execute(
        _exchange_import_identity_select(
            manifest_version, evidence_bundle_id, manifest_digest_hex
        )
    ).scalar_one_or_none()
    if existing is not None:
        return existing, False

    while True:
        record = ExchangeImportRecord(
            id=ids.exchange_import_id(
                manifest_version, evidence_bundle_id, manifest_digest_hex
            ),
            manifest_version=manifest_version,
            evidence_bundle_id=evidence_bundle_id,
            manifest_digest_hex=manifest_digest_hex,
        )
        session.add(record)
        session.add(
            AuditEvent(
                event_type=EVENT_EVIDENCE_BUNDLE_EXCHANGE_IMPORTED,
                resource_id=record.id,
            )
        )
        try:
            session.commit()
        except IntegrityError:
            # A concurrent import registered this identity first: roll back
            # and return that record instead of duplicating it or writing a
            # second audit event.
            session.rollback()
            raced = session.execute(
                _exchange_import_identity_select(
                    manifest_version, evidence_bundle_id, manifest_digest_hex
                )
            ).scalar_one_or_none()
            if raced is None:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
                raise
            return raced, False
        session.refresh(record)
        return record, True


def get_evidence_bundle_exchange_import(
    session: Session, import_id: str
) -> ExchangeImportRecord:
    """Return an exchange-import receipt by id or raise the 404 domain error."""
    record = session.execute(
        select(ExchangeImportRecord).where(ExchangeImportRecord.id == import_id)
    ).scalar_one_or_none()
    if record is None:
        raise EvidenceBundleExchangeImportNotFoundError(import_id)
    return record


def _checkpoint_import_identity_select(
    checkpoint_version: str, event_count: int, events_digest_hex: str
):
    return select(CheckpointImportRecord).where(
        CheckpointImportRecord.checkpoint_version == checkpoint_version,
        CheckpointImportRecord.event_count == event_count,
        CheckpointImportRecord.events_digest_hex == events_digest_hex,
    )


def create_audit_checkpoint_import(
    session: Session,
    payload: AuditCheckpointImportCreate,
) -> tuple[CheckpointImportRecord, bool]:
    """Register one offline-verified audit checkpoint, returning ``(record, created)``.

    The caller has already verified the checkpoint: the request parses under
    the existing checkpoint structure, its event count matches the array,
    and the events digest matches the canonical SHA-256 of the received
    event array exactly as received. This function performs no such
    verification and no local-event lookup: the described events are never
    queried, created, or modified, so whether they exist locally never
    changes the outcome.

    The receiving identity is ``(checkpoint_version, event_count,
    events_digest_hex)``; the event array itself is never stored. A first
    submission writes the receipt row and its
    ``audit.checkpoint_imported`` audit event in a single transaction. A
    retried submission for the same identity returns the existing record
    with ``created=False`` and writes nothing -- no second row and no
    second audit event.
    """
    checkpoint = payload.checkpoint
    checkpoint_version = checkpoint.checkpoint_version
    event_count = checkpoint.event_count
    events_digest_hex = checkpoint.events_digest_hex

    existing = session.execute(
        _checkpoint_import_identity_select(
            checkpoint_version, event_count, events_digest_hex
        )
    ).scalar_one_or_none()
    if existing is not None:
        return existing, False

    while True:
        record = CheckpointImportRecord(
            id=ids.checkpoint_import_id(
                checkpoint_version, event_count, events_digest_hex
            ),
            checkpoint_version=checkpoint_version,
            event_count=event_count,
            events_digest_hex=events_digest_hex,
        )
        session.add(record)
        session.add(
            AuditEvent(
                event_type=EVENT_AUDIT_CHECKPOINT_IMPORTED,
                resource_id=record.id,
            )

class ExchangeImportRecord(Base):
    """An immutable receipt for one offline-verified exchange-bundle package.

    The record is the controlled-import counterpart of the stateless
    verification route: a package whose manifest matches its snapshot under
    the existing canonical SHA-256 rules, and whose snapshot internal
    associations are consistent, is registered exactly once. The receipt
    stores only the receiving identity -- the manifest version, referenced
    evidence bundle id, and manifest digest -- never the snapshot itself and
    never any raw signature, claim payload, content, or evidence bytes; the
    full package must be re-presented on a retry. Verification never depends
    on whether the referenced resources exist locally, so no foreign keys and
    no local resource lookup participate in the decision.

    Records are append-only and immutable; there is deliberately no update
    or delete path. The identity triple is unique, so a retried submission
    for the same package returns the original record without another audit
    event.
    """

    __tablename__ = "evidence_bundle_exchange_imports"
    __table_args__ = (
        UniqueConstraint(
            "manifest_version",
            "evidence_bundle_id",

"""FastAPI application factory.

The database location comes from explicit :class:`~provenance.config.Settings`
(constructor, ``PROVENANCE_DATABASE_URL``, or the CLI flag). Tables are created
automatically on first startup.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import secrets
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

from fastapi import FastAPI

from provenance import __version__
from provenance.api import router as v1_router
from provenance.config import Settings
from provenance.database import (
    init_db,
    make_engine,
    make_session_factory,
)
from provenance.errors import register_exception_handlers


def create_app(settings: Settings | None = None) -> FastAPI:
    settings = settings or Settings.from_env()

    engine = make_engine(settings.database_url)
    # Create tables eagerly so the database is ready as soon as the app exists.
    init_db(engine)
    session_factory = make_session_factory(engine)

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
        # Re-ensure the schema on every startup, not just at factory time:
        # shutdown disposes the engine, and for an in-memory database that
        # drops the whole schema, so a restarted lifespan must recreate the
        # tables before the reused connection serves requests again. The
        # call is idempotent on an already-migrated database.
        init_db(engine)
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            engine.dispose()

    app = FastAPI(
        title="Digital Content Provenance API",
        version=__version__,
        lifespan=lifespan,
    )
    app.state.settings = settings
    app.state.engine = engine
    app.state.session_factory = session_factory
    # Per-process HMAC secrets for opaque pagination cursors. Cursors are
    # stateless and only valid within the process that minted them; a
    # restart rotates the secret and renders outstanding cursors invalid
    # (reported as 422 validation_error) rather than guessable.
    app.state.lineage_cursor_secret = secrets.token_bytes(32)
    app.state.content_evidence_cursor_secret = secrets.token_bytes(32)
    app.state.audit_events_cursor_secret = secrets.token_bytes(32)
    app.state.exchange_imports_cursor_secret = secrets.token_bytes(32)
    app.state.exchange_import_reconciliations_cursor_secret = (
        secrets.token_bytes(32)
    )
    app.state.checkpoint_imports_cursor_secret = secrets.token_bytes(32)
    app.state.checkpoint_import_reconciliations_cursor_secret = (
        secrets.token_bytes(32)
    )
    app.state.claims_cursor_secret = secrets.token_bytes(32)
    app.state.evidence_bundles_cursor_secret = secrets.token_bytes(32)
    app.state.authentication_key_rotations_cursor_secret = (
        secrets.token_bytes(32)
    )
    app.state.attestation_access_grants_cursor_secret = secrets.token_bytes(32)
    app.state.content_export_jobs_cursor_secret = secrets.token_bytes(32)
    app.state.claim_supersession_lineage_cursor_secret = (
        secrets.token_bytes(32)
    )
    app.state.trust_policies_cursor_secret = secrets.token_bytes(32)
    app.state.actors_cursor_secret = secrets.token_bytes(32)
    app.state.contents_cursor_secret = secrets.token_bytes(32)
    app.state.attestation_revocations_cursor_secret = secrets.token_bytes(32)
    app.state.content_relations_cursor_secret = secrets.token_bytes(32)
    app.state.content_coverage_search_cursor_secret = secrets.token_bytes(32)
    app.state.revocation_impacts_cursor_secret = secrets.token_bytes(32)
    app.state.impact_imports_cursor_secret = secrets.token_bytes(32)
    app.state.impact_import_reconciliations_cursor_secret = (
        secrets.token_bytes(32)
    )

    register_exception_handlers(app)
    app.include_router(v1_router)

    @app.get("/healthz", tags=["meta"])
    def healthz() -> dict[str, str]:
        return {"status": "ok"}

    return app

1040	    against the canonical message
1041	    ``["provenance-attestation-v1", target_type, target_id,

1043	    nothing is written. Only the SHA-256 digest of the signature is stored

1047	    signature digest returns the existing attestation with ``created=False``
1048	    and writes no row or audit event. On first creation, the attestation row

1053	    # check the polymorphic target first, then the signing actor.
